# Implementation plan — cancelled CI re-run for issue #4713

Planning ref: `main` at `66707437b53aa54446d661c8f409795577d13ead`. No Integration branch was specified, so there is no known ref mismatch. The earlier Claude progress comments describe work on a separate project branch; this plan targets the checked-out `main`.

Scope-mode: Hold Scope  
Reuse-audit: extends `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml`  
Scope-mode justification: Use the existing PR enumeration and scheduled sweep rather than a new workflow or manual operation. Handling both `cancelled` and `startup_failure`, including a refused re-run, is the complete requested behavior without a new dependency or consumer interface. That favors correctness over a shorter cancelled-only path, consistent with §6 Core Priorities: Security > Correctness & safety > Backward compatibility > Operational clarity > Performance > Speed.

## Automation and wiring

Extend the **30-minute `sweep` job** in `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml`. It already enumerates all open, non-draft PRs; the hourly `claude-pr-catch-all` instead targets `claude/*` fixes. No supervisor, database gate, or future-removal registry entry is needed: the new helper runs only as part of this scheduled job. Wire it **only in coding-workflows**, whose CI workflow is identified as `.github/workflows/ci.yml`; do not assume consumer CI filenames.

## Files likely to change

- `.github/workflows/review_autofix_sweep.yml` — retain its existing dispatch step, add each PR’s current `head.sha` to the enumeration snapshot, and invoke the CI decision helper using a trusted default-branch checkout.
- `scripts/ci_cancelled_rerun.py` — scheduled helper, not a standalone operator script.
- `tests/test_ci_cancelled_rerun.py` — decision, API-call-budget, and workflow-wiring tests.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml`, `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml` — include the focused tests in existing test steps.
- `agents.md`, `README.md`, `docs/INVENTORY.md`, and `changelog.d/4713-ci-cancelled-rerun.md` — register the log prefix and helper, document the switch and behavior, and record the change.

## Functions or modules to implement

Have the existing PR-list call write its snapshot to runner temp; do **not** fetch PRs again. The helper validates the snapshot, applies the existing `head_ref_filter`, `dry_run`, and `[skip ai]` conventions, then selects the newest completed `pull_request` CI run matching each current PR head SHA. Require a valid PR number, SHA, run ID, `status=completed`, conclusion of `cancelled` or `startup_failure`, and `run_attempt == 1`. Never act on `failure`. Skip if another CI run for that head is `queued`, `in_progress`, or `pending`. Log one `CI_CANCELLED_RERUN pr=<n> head=<sha> run=<id> action=<rerun|skip> reason=<…>` decision per examined PR, including missing data and API errors.

The helper’s docstring must state its input/output, fail-closed decision behavior, and **fixed API budget**: one repository-wide completed-run listing (`status=completed&per_page=100`), plus repository-wide active-status listings needed because the completed filter cannot establish that no run is active; no run-list read per PR. Add a comment at those calls explaining why the existing sweep’s review-run cache cannot supply CI state. Use only `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/rerun-failed-jobs` for an eligible run. GitHub documents that endpoint as re-running failed jobs and their dependents, with Actions write permission; its documented success response is `201`. A refused `startup_failure` request is logged, **not** converted into a full-workflow rerun. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2026-03-10))

## Data structures affected

Add `head_sha` to the sweep’s ephemeral PR snapshot. Build an in-memory map of recent CI runs by SHA and an active-run set by SHA. Do not change persistent pipeline state or existing log identifiers; add `CI_CANCELLED_RERUN` to both stable-prefix lists in `agents.md`.

## API/interface changes

Add repository variable `CI_CANCELLED_AUTO_RERUN_ENABLED`, default `true` **inside the helper as well as in workflow wiring**. When false, make no CI API calls or POSTs. Retain existing workflow-dispatch inputs. The workflow already declares `actions: write`; verify the effective token has that permission before relying on it. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2026-03-10))

## Decisions

### D1 — Use the general review sweep
- **Chosen:** Run on the existing 30-minute `sweep` job.
- **Alternatives considered:** The hourly `claude-pr-catch-all` job.
- **Why:** CI recovery applies to every open non-draft PR, not only `claude/*` heads, and the sweep already has the PR snapshot.

### D2 — Re-run failed jobs only
- **Chosen:** Log an API refusal and leave the run untouched.
- **Alternatives considered:** The earlier Claude progress comment proposed falling back to a full rerun for `startup_failure`.
- **Why:** A full rerun conflicts with the issue’s explicit failed-jobs-only method and could re-execute successful jobs.

### D3 — Bound CI reads by repository, not PR
- **Chosen:** Use one completed listing and fixed-count active-status listings, matched locally to the existing PR snapshot.
- **Alternatives considered:** Fetching CI history separately for each PR.
- **Why:** Active runs cannot be inferred from a `status=completed` result; fixed-count listings preserve the requested rate-limit shape. GitHub’s workflow-runs endpoint supports the workflow filename, status filters, and `per_page=100`. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs?apiVersion=2026-03-10))

## Security considerations

The scheduled job crosses from author-controlled PR metadata into an Actions write operation. Validate identifiers before constructing an API path, match the *current* PR head rather than a superseded commit, accept only the identified `ci.yml` workflow’s PR runs, and never execute code checked out from a PR head. Check out the trusted default-branch copy of the helper with credentials not persisted. Keep API errors and malformed or incomplete snapshots non-mutating; do not print tokens or response bodies. No new public endpoint or money-handling surface is introduced. Abuse cases to test include a forged snapshot run ID, an old cancelled head, a concurrent active run, and an untrusted branch supplying helper code.

## Risks and edge cases

- GitHub documents `GITHUB_SHA` for a `pull_request` workflow as the merge-branch commit. Match the workflow-run API’s **validated `head_sha` field** to the PR snapshot rather than assuming the job’s `GITHUB_SHA` is its head; skip an unmatchable run. ([docs.github.com](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows))
- `run_attempt` is **per workflow run**, not intrinsically per head. Selecting only the newest matching run and rejecting a visible same-head attempt 2 prevents ordinary repeat ticks, but a bounded 100-run listing cannot prove that an older, no-longer-visible *different run* on the same head was previously retried. Document this limitation explicitly; do not claim a durable, absolute per-head guarantee from `run_attempt` alone.
- A `startup_failure` may have no failed jobs for the endpoint to restart. Log the refusal and leave it for the next supported recovery path; do not silently broaden to a full rerun.
- A head push or manually initiated re-run can race the snapshot. Active-run evidence or ambiguity must suppress the POST; a failed POST must not be logged as success.

## Testing considerations

Mock listings and POSTs for cancelled attempt 1, attempt 2, `failure`, `startup_failure`, superseded SHA, active CI, and disabled switch. Also cover malformed IDs, missing or partial API data, no matching run, dry-run/filter behavior, a refused POST without full-rerun fallback, and multiple same-head runs. Assert fixed-count CI listings, no per-PR run reads, and the trusted checkout and permissions wiring. Run the focused tests, existing sweep contract tests, workflow lint, and the workflow-size guard; measure the changed YAML with `wc -c` (its inspected baseline is 21,506 bytes, below the 480,000-byte guard).

PLAN_SELF_CHECK: WARNING: `run_attempt` alone cannot establish an absolute per-head cap across distinct CI run IDs outside the bounded listing; the implementer must preserve the stated conservative behavior and document that limit.
